newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Vefa cuts rates, aims for $100 mln prft.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Vefa cuts rates, aims for $100 mln prft.

text.p: Albania's Vefa Holding group will cut interest rates at its loan-taking scheme from eight to five percent and aims to turn in a profit of some $100 million in 1997, an Albanian paper said on Friday.

Vehbi Alimuca, head of the group with interests in 240 businesses ranging from supermarkets through to mines and tourist agencies, told daily Koha Jone: "lowering interest to five percent....is to offer a better guarantee to citizens depositing in these investment schemes."

Alleged pyramid schemes have drawn millions of dollars over the past years from depositors in Europe's poorest nation, sucking vast sums of money out from the banking system and alarming world finance bodies.
Some schemes promise interest of up to 50 percent.
One of the schemes recently collapsed owing $13 million to depositors and two others have suspended payments.
Vefa's new rates, effective on Friday, will be the lowest on offer in Albania.
An Albanian opposition party on Thursday repeated claims that firms running get-rich-quick schemes had given financial support to the ruling Democratic Party, which denies this.
The Albanian lek continued to weaken against the U.S. dollar on Friday as investors in such get-rich-quick schemes rushed to switch their returns into hard currency rather than to reinvest.
